question.text: Kalinga Capital (Cat II AIF) adds a new LP, Mr. Rohan Gupta, who commits INR 85 lakh. Mr. Gupta is NOT an Accredited Investor. Has the AIF complied with the minimum investment norm under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Yes, because INR 85 lakh exceeds the INR 25 lakh minimum.
Yes, because the 75% investor-value threshold was met.
Yes, because the fund size is a private matter between GP and LPs.
No — the minimum investment from every non-Accredited investor must be at least INR 1 crore.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.83, 285 and 342 (Regulation 10 with the Accredited Investor carve-out): 'Minimum investment amount from every investor should be INR 1 crore', except where the Accredited Investor exemption applies. Mr. Gupta's INR 85 lakh commitment from a non-Accredited investor is a compliance breach, so the keyed non-compliance answer is correct. The Trap: The INR 25 lakh figure in the source applies to employees/directors of the AIF or Manager — not the Angel Fund minimum (angel investors in Angel Funds have no specified minimum). 75% by value is the winding-up threshold, unrelated. Privacy is not a compliance defence. Note: Corrected the INR 25 lakh carve-out explanation, which previously mis-stated the Angel Fund position. Removed the fund-raising-screening pro-tip and the Cross-Exam Context paragraph as broader than the source.
